title: Batman's First Appearance
description: Detective Comics #27 — The Case of the Chemical Syndicate. Batman's debut in May 1939, written by Bill Finger and drawn by Bob Kane.

title: The Origin of Batman
description: Detective Comics #33 establishes Batman's origin: young Bruce Wayne witnesses his parents' murder and vows vengeance, training his body and mind to become the Batman.

title: Batman: Year One
description: Frank Miller and David Mazzucchelli's reimagining of Batman's first year — gritty, realistic, and definitively modern. Batman #404-407 (1987).

title: Batman: Year Three
description: Jim Aparo and Marv Wolfman's retelling of Dick Grayson's origin as Robin — the murder of his parents by Tony Zucco, Bruce taking him in, and the events that shaped their partnership. Bridges directly into A Lonely Place of Dying.

title: Jason Todd Becomes Robin
description: Jason Todd's first adventures in the Robin costume alongside Batman, establishing the new Dynamic Duo after Dick Grayson's departure. Batman #366-368.

title: Letting Go
description: Bruce Wayne confronts Dick Grayson and effectively fires him as Robin after years of growing distance and resentment. The definitive break between Batman and his first partner, setting Dick on the path to becoming Nightwing.

title: The Killing Joke
description: Alan Moore and Brian Bolland's landmark one-shot — the Joker shoots Barbara Gordon through the spine, paralyzing her, then abducts and tortures Commissioner Gordon to prove that one bad day can drive anyone insane. Barbara's paralysis becomes the catalyst for her reinvention as Oracle.

title: A Death in the Family Prelude
description: The issues leading directly into A Death in the Family showing Jason becoming increasingly reckless, angry, and difficult to control — setting up his tragic death. Batman #422-425.

title: A Death in the Family
description: The Joker beats Jason Todd (Robin II) to death with a crowbar, then kills him with a bomb. Batman arrives too late. One of the most consequential stories in comics history — the death decided by reader phone-in vote.

title: A Lonely Place of Dying
description: Tim Drake deduces Batman's identity and forces himself into Bruce's life as the new Robin. Introduces the third and most celebrated Robin.

title: Tim Drake Becomes Robin
description: Tim Drake officially dons the Robin costume for the first time — Batman #457-458. Having deduced Batman's identity and proven himself, Tim earns the right to be Robin and begins his training under Bruce.

title: Knightfall
description: Bane orchestrates the release of Arkham's inmates, exhausts Batman, then breaks his back. Jean-Paul Valley (Azrael) takes the mantle. Batman #484-500, Detective Comics #654-666 (1993).

title: Knightquest
description: Jean-Paul Valley operates as a brutal, increasingly unhinged Batman while Bruce Wayne heals. Batman #501-508, Detective Comics #667-675 (1993-1994).

title: KnightsEnd
description: Bruce Wayne, healed and retrained by Lady Shiva, reclaims the Batman mantle from the out-of-control Azrael. Batman #509-515, Detective Comics #676-681 (1994).

title: No Man's Land
description: After a catastrophic earthquake, the US government abandons Gotham. Batman must reclaim his city one block at a time across an entire year of comics (1999).

title: Hush
description: Jeph Loeb and Jim Lee's blockbuster 12-part story pitting Batman against every major villain as a mysterious new enemy called Hush manipulates events from the shadows. Batman #608-619 (2002-2003).

title: Under the Hood
description: A mysterious new Red Hood emerges in Gotham — a brutal vigilante who kills criminals and knows Batman's secrets. Batman #635-641. The definitive Jason Todd return story culminating in his unmasking in #638.

title: War Games
description: A gang war engulfs Gotham. Stephanie Brown briefly becomes Robin before being captured and killed by Black Mask. Tim's tenure as Robin effectively ends here. Batman #631-633.

title: Batman and Son
description: Grant Morrison introduces Damian Wayne — Bruce's son with Talia al Ghul — to the mainline DC universe. Batman #655-658 (2006).

title: Batman R.I.P.
description: Grant Morrison's culmination of his Batman run — Dr. Hurt and the Black Glove attempt to destroy Batman psychologically and physically. Batman #676-681 (2008).

title: Battle for the Cowl
description: After Bruce Wayne's apparent death in Final Crisis, the Bat-family fractures as multiple people vie for the Batman mantle. Dick Grayson ultimately accepts the responsibility.

title: Batman Reborn
description: Dick Grayson's debut as Batman alongside Damian Wayne as Robin. Their first case against Professor Pyg's Circus of Strange establishes the new dynamic duo's inverted dynamic — a lighter Batman and a darker Robin.

title: Revenge of the Red Hood
description: Jason Todd returns as the Red Hood with a new female sidekick Scarlet, executing criminals and challenging Dick Grayson's Batman on his methods.

title: Batman and Robin Must Die
description: Morrison's culmination of the Batman and Robin series — Doctor Hurt returns to destroy the Batman legacy once and for all while Bruce Wayne begins his return through time.

title: The Return of Bruce Wayne
description: Bruce Wayne unstuck in time — traveling from prehistoric Gotham through Puritan, pirate, western, and noir detective eras before returning to the present as a living weapon against Darkseid.

title: Batman Incorporated: Leviathan
description: Morrison's grand finale — Talia al Ghul's Leviathan wages all-out war against Batman Incorporated, leading to Damian Wayne's death at the hands of the Heretic.

title: The Black Mirror
description: Scott Snyder's pre-New 52 Detective Comics run with Dick Grayson as Batman facing Commissioner Gordon's son James Jr. as a psychopath. Detective Comics #871-881 (2011).

title: Faces of Death
description: Tony S. Daniel's New 52 Detective Comics debut — Batman hunts the Gotham Ripper while the Joker and Dollmaker lurk in the shadows. Det Comics Vol 2 #1-7.

title: The Court of Owls
description: Scott Snyder and Greg Capullo's landmark New 52 debut — Batman discovers a centuries-old secret society controlling Gotham and their undead assassins the Talons. Batman (Vol 2) #1-11 (2011-2012).

title: Night of the Owls
description: The Court of Owls unleashes their Talons across Gotham in a coordinated strike against Batman and his allies. Batman (Vol 2) #8-9 crossover (2012).

title: Emperor Penguin
description: John Layman's debut arc — the Penguin's lieutenant Ogilvy stages a coup and becomes Emperor Penguin while the real Penguin is imprisoned. Det Comics Vol 2 #13-18.

title: Death of the Family
description: The Joker returns with his face cut off, targeting every member of the Bat-family to prove they make Batman weak. Batman (Vol 2) #13-17 (2012-2013).

title: Icarus
description: Batman investigates a deadly new drug called Icarus flooding Gotham's streets in John Layman's second major arc. Det Comics Vol 2 #20-24.

title: Zero Year
description: Snyder and Capullo's New 52 reimagining of Batman's origin — a 12-part epic that rewrites Bruce's early years and first encounters with the Riddler and Red Hood Gang. Batman (Vol 2) #21-33 (2013-2014).

title: Endgame
description: The Joker returns with a biological weapon claiming to be ancient and immortal. Batman and Joker apparently kill each other beneath Gotham. Batman (Vol 2) #35-40 (2014-2015).

title: Superheavy
description: With Bruce Wayne amnesiac and happy, Jim Gordon dons a Batman suit to protect Gotham. A bold status quo change exploring what Batman means without Bruce Wayne. Batman (Vol 2) #41-50 (2015-2016).

title: Rise of the Batmen
description: James Tynion IV's Rebirth debut — Batman and Batwoman assemble a team of Gotham vigilantes to fight the Colony, a paramilitary group using Batman's technology. Det Comics #934-940.

title: I Am Gotham
description: Tom King's debut arc introduces Gotham and Gotham Girl — two new heroes with Superman-level powers whose idealism clashes with Batman's darker methods. Batman (Vol 3) #1-6 (2016).

title: I Am Suicide
description: Batman assembles a Suicide Squad-style team to infiltrate Santa Prisca and steal from Bane. King's spy-thriller approach to Batman mythology. Batman (Vol 3) #7-12 (2016-2017).

title: I Am Bane
description: Bane comes to Gotham to reclaim Psycho-Pirate, leading to one of the most brutal Batman vs. Bane fights in comics history. Batman (Vol 3) #13-17 (2017).

title: The War of Jokes and Riddles
description: Set in Year Two of Batman's career, the Joker and Riddler go to war over the right to kill Batman, dragging all of Gotham into their conflict. Batman (Vol 3) #25-32 (2017).

title: The Victim Syndicate
description: A group of people scarred by Batman's war on crime blame the Dark Knight for their suffering and target his allies. Det Comics #943-947.

title: League of Shadows
description: Ra's al Ghul's splinter faction the League of Shadows targets Gotham for destruction, forcing Batman and Batwoman to confront their differences. Det Comics #950-956.

title: A Lonely Place of Living
description: Tim Drake is rescued from a time trap by a future version of himself gone wrong — a pivotal story for the Red Robin character. Det Comics #963-968.

title: The Wedding
description: Tom King's culmination of the Bruce/Selina romance — Batman proposes to Catwoman. The wedding issue (#50) becomes one of the era's most discussed comics. Batman (Vol 3) #33-50 (2018).

title: Fall of the Batmen
description: The Belfry team fractures as secrets surface — Clayface's loyalty is tested and the team faces its most personal crisis yet. Det Comics #970-975.

title: Batmen Eternal
description: Tynion's finale — the Gotham Knights face dissolution as Batman questions the entire experiment of training young heroes. Det Comics #976-981.

title: City of Bane
description: Bane takes over Gotham City, installing Thomas Wayne as Batman and breaking the Bat-family. Tom King's epic conclusion to his 85-issue run. Batman (Vol 3) #72-85 (2019-2020).

title: The Joker War
description: The Joker acquires Wayne Enterprises' resources and weaponizes Gotham against Batman. James Tynion IV's debut arc. Batman (Vol 3) #95-100 (2020).

title: Fear State
description: The Scarecrow orchestrates a citywide fear toxin attack as the anti-tech Magistrate program takes over Gotham. Batman (Vol 3) #105-110 (2021).

title: Deface the Face
description: Peter Tomasi's debut arc on Detective Comics — Batman investigates a series of murders targeting Gotham's disfigured villains. Det Comics #994-999.

title: Failsafe
description: Chip Zdarsky's debut arc — an unstoppable robot built by Batman himself to stop him if he ever kills targets the Dark Knight. Batman (Vol 3) #125-130 (2023).
